mainTopic: Higher כתובות for priestly and distinguished families, and the bride's claim about losing her virginity, tied to בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: the court raised the כתובה of a כהן's widow to two hundred, then lowered it again when men stopped marrying those widows. Next, רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that distinguished Israelite families may also demand a higher כתובה, like the כהנים. A ברייתא seems to limit this to marriages involving a כהן. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא uses a 'לא מבעיא' style and teaches the harder case. Then a new משנה brings a case: a husband finds his bride is not a virgin, she says it happened after betrothal, and he says before. רבן גמליאל believes her, and רבי יהושע requires proof. The גמרא connects this to a money argument, 'you owe me' against 'I don't know', where one side holds בָּרִי עָדִיף and the other holds that money stays with its owner. The גמרא suggests the two arguments are the same, but shows that רב נחמן can agree with רבן גמליאל because the bride had a מיגו or a חזקה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a proof that רב נחמן follows רבן גמליאל, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the widow's כתובה went up and then came back down
steps.stepSummary: The court first raised the כתובה of a כהן's widow to two hundred so people would respect her. When men stopped marrying such widows, the court returned to the original amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the court saw that the כהנים were treating these widows with disrespect, they set a כתובה of two hundred for them. But then they saw that men were avoiding them. The men said: 'Instead of marrying a כהן's widow for that price, let's go marry a young Israelite girl who has never been married.' So the court put things back the way they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to an earlier contradiction about the כתובה of a כהן's widow. It explains that the two sources describe two different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source gives the widow of a כהן a higher amount and another gives a lower one. The answer is that the court changed the rule twice. It raised the amount to protect her dignity, then lowered it again because the higher amount hurt her chances of marrying. So the sources do not really argue; each one describes a different period.

keyTerms.meaning: treating with disrespect, belittling
they instituted (a rabbinic enactment, תקנה)
two hundred (זוז), the כתובה amount of a בתולה
pulling away, staying away
a widow from a priestly family
they returned things to how they were before

steps.whatToRemember: The court can adjust a תקנה when it backfires. Raising the widow's כתובה was meant to help her, but once it kept her from getting married, the court undid it.

phrases.english: Once they saw that they were treating them with disrespect,
phrases.notes: 'They' is the court, and 'them' is the widows, whom the כהנים were treating lightly.

phrases.english: they instituted for them two hundred.
Once they saw that they were staying away from them,
as they said: Rather than marrying a widow of priests,
let us go marry a virgin Israelite woman,
phrases.notes: The price is the same, so the men preferred a never-married girl.

phrases.english: they returned things to their original state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the contradiction raised on the previous section of the daf, about the כתובה of a priestly widow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two time periods: each source reflects a different stage of the court's enactments.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to contradict each other about the widow's amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: The amount was raised to two hundred and later returned to its original level, so each source describes a different period.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The higher amount for a כהן's widow was temporary and was undone because it discouraged men from marrying her.

steps.title: Distinguished Israelite families may also demand a higher כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's 'court of כהנים', רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that distinguished Israelite families may also follow the כהנים' practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A court of כהנים...' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was not said only about a court of כהנים. Even Israelite families with distinguished lineage may act the way the כהנים do, if they want to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about the court of כהנים collecting a higher כתובה for their daughters. שמואל extends that practice to distinguished families who are not כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions only כהנים. שמואל teaches that the real reason is family prestige, not כהונה itself. So any family with a proven, respected lineage may set a higher כתובה for its daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: the court of the כהנים, which collected four hundred for a priestly בתולה
families with a distinguished, proven lineage
following the same practice the כהנים follow

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the test case for the rest of this section: does the higher כתובה belong to כהונה, or to any distinguished family?

phrases.english: "A court of priests," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says their court collected four hundred for a priest's virgin daughter.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ,
phrases.english: They did not say this only about a court of priests,
but even families of distinguished lineage in Israel,
if they wanted to act
the way the priests act, they may act so.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Distinguished Israelite families may demand a higher כתובה for their daughters, just as the כהנים do.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to limit the practice to marriages involving a כהן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists only cases with a כהן on one side, which suggests that two plain Israelites may not use the higher amount. This seems to go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: Whoever wants to act like the כהנים, for example an Israelite woman marrying a כהן or a כהן's daughter marrying an Israelite, may do so. The גמרא reads this closely: those are cases where a כהן is involved. But an Israelite woman marrying an Israelite man? No!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא. Every example in the ברייתא includes a כהן, so it seems to rule out a marriage between two Israelites.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge works by reading the ברייתא's examples closely. If the ברייתא only allows cases with a 'צד כהונה', then a distinguished Israelite family marrying another Israelite would not qualify. That would contradict שמואל's broad ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
some connection to כהונה on one side of the marriage
for example

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who wants to act the way the priests act,
such as an Israelite woman marrying a priest,
or a priest's daughter marrying an Israelite, may act so.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן וּבַת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: An Israelite woman to a priest and a priest's daughter to an Israelite,
that is where there is some side of priesthood.
But an Israelite woman to an Israelite man, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים עוֹשִׂין
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that distinguished Israelite families may act like the כהנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's examples all include a כהן. This implies that a marriage of two Israelites cannot use the higher כתובה, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The ברייתא is teaching a bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses a 'לא מבעיא' style. Two Israelites is the obvious case. The ברייתא teaches the harder case, where the husband is a כהן and could claim he is already raising her status.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say this about an Israelite woman marrying an Israelite man. He cannot tell her, 'I am raising your status,' so of course her family can ask for more. But with an Israelite woman marrying a כהן, he can tell her, 'I am raising your status.' You might have thought she cannot ask for more. So the ברייתא teaches us that she can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It says the ברייתא skipped the plain Israelite case because it is obvious, and chose a harder case to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a woman marries a כהן, he could argue that marrying into כהונה is already a gain for her, so she should not demand extra money. The ברייתא teaches that even so, her distinguished family may demand the higher כתובה. The plain Israelite case is allowed even more, so the ברייתא actually supports שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: it is speaking in a 'no need to say' style, teaching the harder case
'I am raising your status' (by marrying you)
I might have said no
it teaches us (something new)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'בת ישראל' in this answer is a woman from a distinguished family. The ברייתא did not leave out the Israelite-to-Israelite case because it is forbidden. It left it out because it is too obvious to need saying.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל stands: any distinguished family may demand a higher כתובה. The ברייתא chose the harder case, a woman marrying a כהן, to show that even there she may demand it.

phrases.english: It is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
There is no need to say an Israelite woman marrying an Israelite,
phrases.notes: He means a woman from a distinguished Israelite family.

phrases.english: where he cannot say to her:
I am raising your status,
but an Israelite woman marrying a priest,
where he can say to her:
I am raising your status,
I might say no; so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: 'לא מבעיא', where the stated case is the harder one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists only cases with a כהן, so the plain Israelite case seemed excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plain Israelite case is obvious. The ברייתא teaches that even a woman marrying a כהן may demand a higher כתובה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's ruling stands: distinguished Israelite families may set a higher כתובה.

steps.title: The case: a bride who is not a virgin, and two opposite claims
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new topic. A husband finds his bride is not a virgin. She says it happened after betrothal, and he says it happened before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man marries a woman and finds she is not a virgin. She says: I was raped after you betrothed me, so this is your bad luck. He says: No, it happened before I betrothed you, so our marriage deal was made by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a case where the wife and the husband give opposite stories. This step only gives the claims. The rulings come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Timing is everything here. If it happened after betrothal, she was already his wife and it is his loss, so she keeps her כתובה. If it happened before, he married her under a false belief, so the deal is a מקח טעות and she may lose her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
His field was flooded, a way of saying 'this is your bad luck'
A mistaken deal, made on a false belief, so it can be cancelled

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who marries a woman
and did not find her to be a virgin.
She says: After you betrothed me, I was raped,
and his field was flooded.
phrases.notes: This is a saying. The bad luck hit the husband's own 'field,' so the loss is his.

phrases.english: And he says: Not so,
rather, it happened before I betrothed you,
and my acquisition was a mistaken acquisition —

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וְלֹא מָצָא לָהּ בְּתוּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about the כתובה of a כהן's widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: she claims it happened after betrothal, and he claims it happened before.

steps.title: The dispute: is the bride believed?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. רבי יהושע says she is presumed to have lost her virginity before betrothal unless she brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say: She is believed. רבי יהושע says: We don't go by what she says. We assume this happened before betrothal and she misled him, until she brings proof for her claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the two opinions on whose story we accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל trusts her word. רבי יהושע puts the burden of proof on her. Without proof, we assume the worse case: it happened before betrothal and she tricked him.

keyTerms.meaning: She is believed
The assumption that she already had relations (before betrothal)
Proof

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the גמרא tries to find the reason behind רבן גמליאל's view. It ties his view to the rule that a certain claim beats an unsure one.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: We do not live by what comes out of her mouth,
phrases.notes: He means: we don't decide this case based only on her word.

phrases.english: rather, she is presumed to have had relations
before she was betrothed, and she misled him,
until she brings proof for her words.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings on the case set up in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר: she is believed. רבי יהושע: she is not believed without proof.

steps.title: A money dispute: 'You owe me' versus 'I don't know'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings an argument about a person who answers a money claim with 'I don't know.' רב יהודה and רב הונא say he must pay. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: One person says, 'You have a מנה of mine.' The other says, 'I don't know.' רב יהודה and רב הונא say: He must pay. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say: He is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a related argument from the world of money claims. It will use this argument to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case has the same shape as the משנה. One side is sure, and the other side is unsure. The question is whether being sure is enough to win against someone who is holding the money.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, an opening for an argument between אמוראים
A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
Obligated to pay
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
"I have a maneh in your hand,"
phrases.notes: In other words: 'You owe me a hundred זוז.'

phrases.english: and the other says: I don't know —

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי: חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda and Rav Huna say: He is obligated,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי: פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: and Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan say: He is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: מָנֶה לִי בְּיָדְךָ וְהַלָּה אוֹמֵר אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel money dispute that will be used to explain the argument in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה and רב הונא: the 'I don't know' person pays. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן: he is exempt.

steps.title: The reasons: certain beats unsure, or money stays with its owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both sides. One side holds that a certain claim wins. The other holds that money stays where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב יהודה say he must pay, because when one side is certain and the other is unsure, certain wins. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say he is exempt, because we leave the money with the person who has it now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each opinion from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are two opposite rules. בָּרִי עָדִיף means a sure claim beats an unsure one. אוֹקִי מָמוֹנָא בְּחֶזְקַת מָרֵיהּ means the person holding the money keeps it unless the claimant proves his case. Each side is choosing which rule is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain versus maybe, and certain wins
Leave the money with its current owner

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules clash here. בָּרִי עָדִיף says a sure claim wins. אוֹקִי מָמוֹנָא בְּחֶזְקַת מָרֵיהּ says the person holding the money keeps it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמְרִי חַיָּיב —
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda say he is obligated —
when it is 'certain' against 'maybe,' 'certain' is better.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי פָּטוּר —
phrases.english: Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan say he is exempt —
leave the money in the possession of its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two opinions given in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Obligated because בָּרִי עָדִיף. Exempt because the money stays with its holder.

steps.title: אביי: this is already שמואל's view
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the view of רב הונא and רב יהודה matches שמואל. שמואל ruled like רבן גמליאל, who believes a pregnant woman's certain claim about who the father is.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: The view of רב הונא and רב יהודה is really שמואל's view. We learned in a משנה: An unmarried woman was pregnant. They asked her who the father is, and she said: a certain man, and he is a כהן. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי links the 'certain wins' opinion to an earlier authority, שמואל, through a משנה that comes a little later in our פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pregnant woman case, רבן גמליאל believes her sure claim about the father. Since שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל, אביי reasons that שמואל also holds בָּרִי עָדִיף. So the view of רב הונא and רב יהודה already has שמואל behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Pregnant
What is its nature? Here: who is the father?
The הלכה follows (this opinion)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה — דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הִיא.
phrases.english: This view of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda — it is Shmuel's.
As we learned: If she was pregnant,
phrases.notes: This משנה appears a little further on, on דף י״ג.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל עוּבָּר זֶה?
phrases.english: and they said to her: What is the nature of this fetus?
She answered: It is from so-and-so, and he is a priest —

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Eliezer say: She is believed.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה דִּשְׁמוּאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the 'certain wins' view from step 8 by tying it to שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רב הונא and רב יהודה that בָּרִי עָדִיף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל, who believes the pregnant woman's certain claim.

steps.title: A stronger link: שמואל ruled like רבן גמליאל 'even in the first case'
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reminds רב יהודה that שמואל ruled like רבן גמליאל even in the first case, which is our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, you told us in שמואל's name that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל even in the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of שמואל is brought. It extends his ruling to our משנה, the first in the series of these disputes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה, the 'first' case, is about a כתובה, so money is at stake. That makes it closer to the 'I don't know' money case than the pregnant woman case. So this report is a stronger link between שמואל and בָּרִי עָדִיף.

keyTerms.meaning: A friendly nickname, literally 'big-toothed one' (sharp one)
In the name of...
Even in the first (case)

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said to Rav Yehuda:
Big-toothed one, you told us in Shmuel's name:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel even in the first case.
phrases.notes: 'The first case' is our משנה, the first in a row of similar disputes in this פרק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to אביי's link by showing that שמואל ruled like רבן גמליאל in our money-related משנה too.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל holds בָּרִי עָדִיף, even in money matters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's report that שמואל ruled like רבן גמליאל 'even in the first case.'

steps.title: What does 'even in the first case' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is special about the first case, so that the word 'even' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'even in the first case' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the word 'even.' It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even' means the first case is harder for רבן גמליאל than the others. The גמרא wants to know what makes it harder.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'even in the first case'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to explain the wording of the report in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first case is a bigger test for רבן גמליאל's view.

steps.title: In the first case, certain wins even against keeping money with its owner
steps.stepSummary: The first case is special because money is involved, and one could say 'leave the money with its owner.' Even so, רבן גמליאל said a certain claim wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though one could say 'leave the money with its owner,' רבן גמליאל said: certain wins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. In our משנה, רבן גמליאל let the bride's certain claim beat the rule that money stays with its holder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband holds the money of the כתובה, so normally it would stay with him. רבן גמליאל still believes the bride because her claim is certain and his is only a guess. That is exactly the view of רב הונא and רב יהודה, so שמואל agrees with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
There is room to say

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, רבן גמליאל holds that בָּרִי עָדִיף even in a money case, against אוֹקִי מָמוֹנָא בְּחֶזְקַת מָרֵיהּ. This supports רב הונא and רב יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'owner' of the money here is the husband, because he is holding it. The bride is the one claiming, yet she still wins because her claim is certain.

phrases.english: Even though there is room to say
'leave the money in the possession of its owner' —
Rabban Gamliel said: Certain is better.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר אוֹקֵי מָמוֹנָא בְּחֶזְקַת מָרֵיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first case involves money held by the husband, and רבן גמליאל still rules that the bride's certain claim wins.

steps.title: Is the money case the same argument as רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב יהודה and רב הונא follow רבן גמליאל, while רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן follow רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יהודה and רב הונא hold like רבן גמליאל, and רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן hold like רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to tie the money argument to the older argument in our משנה. This sets up the next move, where the idea will be pushed back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל trusts a certain claim, so he seems to match רב יהודה and רב הונא, who say a certain claim wins over 'I don't know.' רבי יהושע leaves things as they are, so he seems to match רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן, who say the money stays with its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A suggestion the גמרא often goes on to reject
The תנא who argues with רבן גמליאל and does not accept the bride's claim
An אמורא who holds that the money stays with its owner

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Yehuda and Rav Huna
who say [a certain claim wins] hold like Rabban Gamliel,
and Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan
who say [the money stays put] hold like Rabbi Yehoshua?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 9 to 12, which linked רב יהודה's view to רבן גמליאל, and now proposes that the whole argument is just the תנאים' argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the אמוראים' argument about בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא really the same as the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע?

steps.title: רב נחמן can agree with רבן גמליאל because the bride had a מיגו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבן גמליאל believed the bride only because she had a מיגו, and in the money case there is no מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן can tell you: What I said fits even רבן גמליאל. רבן גמליאל only said his ruling there, where there is a מיגו. But here, what מיגו is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רב נחמן does not have to argue with רבן גמליאל, because the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the bride had an extra reason to be believed: she could have made a stronger claim and did not. That is a מיגו. The person claiming money has no such extra support, so even רבן גמליאל would not trust his claim alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he could have made a better claim, we believe the claim he did make
He only said his ruling in this specific situation
There (the משנה's case) / here (the money case)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying רבן גמליאל is wrong. He is saying רבן גמליאל's ruling never reached the money case at all.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman can say to you:
What I said fits even Rabban Gamliel's view.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel only said his ruling there
because there is a מיגו.
phrases.notes: The bride could have made a better claim, like saying it was an accident with wood. She didn't, so we trust what she did say.

phrases.english: But here, what מיגו is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב נַחְמָן: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי, אֲפִילּוּ כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 13's suggestion that רב נחמן must hold like רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the אמוראים' argument depends on the תנאים' argument.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored that the bride had a מיגו supporting her, which the money claimant does not have.

steps.title: A second answer: the bride had a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: Or רב נחמן could say that רבן גמליאל believed the bride because she kept her חזקה, and the money claimant has no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: רבן גמליאל only said his ruling there, where we say 'leave her in her חזקה.' But here, what חזקה does this person have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why the bride's case is not like the money case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bride was assumed to be a proper virgin bride, and her claim keeps that status in place. The person demanding money has no status in his favor. He is trying to take money that is not in his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Or else; another possible answer
A status we assume until it is proven otherwise
Leave her in her assumed status

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons why רבן גמליאל's ruling does not reach the money case: the bride has a מיגו, or the bride has a חזקה. The money claimant has neither.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם
phrases.english: Or else: Rabban Gamliel only said his ruling there
where we say, 'Leave her in her assumed status,'
phrases.notes: Her status is that she was a proper virgin bride. The husband is the one trying to change it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, מַאי חֲזָקָה אִית לֵיהּ לְהַאי?
phrases.english: but here, what assumed status does this person have?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם אֶלָּא דְּאָמְרִינַן אוֹקְמַהּ אַחֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative reason for the same rejection made in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Again rejects linking רב נחמן to רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bride's claim is backed by a חזקה, while the money claimant has none.

steps.title: It makes sense that רב נחמן holds like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the way it answered is also logical, because רב נחמן is the one who rules like רבן גמליאל. A proof follows next.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, the way we answered, that רב נחמן is the one who rules like רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to support its answer. This line sets up a proof that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב נחמן himself rules like רבן גמליאל, then he cannot be relying on רבי יהושע in the money case. That backs up the answers in steps 14 and 15, which said the two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense; this opens a supporting proof
The way we answered

phrases.english: So too it makes sense
the way we answered,
phrases.notes: He means the answers in steps 14 and 15: the money case is different from the bride's case.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב נַחְמָן הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: that it is Rav Nachman who rules like Rabban Gamliel,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejections in steps 14 and 15 by showing that רב נחמן himself follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן agrees with רבן גמליאל and does not depend on רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's own ruling like רבן גמליאל, which is brought in the lines that follow.
